title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
keyIdea: A window can become all one letter if (length − count of its most common letter) ≤ k. Grow the window with j, slide i while that cost is over k, and keep the largest window. maxCount may go stale (never decreases), which only stops the window from growing, never gives a wrong answer.

approaches.name: Brute force: every window
approaches.idea: For each start i, extend j with a fresh count array and check length − maxCount ≤ k.
approaches.why: n starts × up to n ends.

approaches.name: Sliding window with maxCount
approaches.idea: freq[s[j]]++, maxCount = max(maxCount, freq[s[j]]); while (len − maxCount > k) shrink from i; maxLen = max(maxLen, len).
approaches.why: j moves n times, i at most n times; the map holds at most 26 letters.

quiz.q: How many replacements does a window need?
options: length − count of its most frequent letter

quiz.q: Why is it OK that maxCount is never decreased?
options: A stale maxCount only makes the window slide instead of grow; the answer only improves when a truly bigger maxCount appears
It's a bug that happens to pass
